courses.title: Junior Symposium
courses.description: Laboratory, three hours. Course 101A is enforced requisite to 101B, which is enforced requisite to 101C. Limited to Film and Television majors. courses.title: History of European Motion Picture
courses.description: Lecture/screenings, six hours; discussion, one hour. Historical and critical survey, with examples, of European motion picture both as developing art form and as medium of mass communication. Letter grading.

courses.title: History of African, Asian, and Latin American Film
courses.description: Lecture/screenings, six hours; discussion, one hour. Critical, historical, aesthetic, and social study—together with exploration of ethnic significance—of Asian, African, Latin American, and Mexican films. Letter grading.

courses.title: Experimental Film
courses.description: Lecture/screenings, six hours; discussion, one hour. Study and analysis of unconventional developments in motion pictures. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: History of Documentary Film
courses.description: Lecture/screenings, six hours; discussion, one hour. Philosophy of documentary approach in motion pictures. Development of critical standards and examination of techniques of teaching and persuasion used in selected documentary, educational, and propaganda films. Letter grading.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Documentary: New Documentary Forms
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour; screenings, three hours. Examination of today’s documentary modes of representation and genres focusing on rise and diversification of nonfiction modes since new millennium. From short form to series based, virtual reality to interactive, crowd sourced to animated, study of new documentary forms and platforms… For more content click the Read More button below.

courses.title: American Television History
courses.description: Lecture/screenings, four hours; discussion, one hour. Critical survey of American television history from its inception to present. Examination of interrelationships between program forms, industrial paradigms, social trends, and culture. Starting with television’s hybrid origins in radio, theater, and film, contextualization, viewing, and discussion of key television shows, as well as… For more content click the Read More button below.

courses.title: Film and Social Change
courses.description: Lecture/screenings, six hours; discussion, one hour. Development of documentary and dramatic films in relation to and as force in social development. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Film Authors
courses.description: Lecture/screenings, four hours; discussion, one hour. In-depth study of specific film author (director or writer). May be repeated for credit with topic change. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Film Genres
courses.description: Lecture/screenings, four hours; discussion, one hour. Study of specific film genre (e.g., Western, gangster cycle, musical, silent epic, comedy, social drama). May be repeated for credit with topic change. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: History of Animation in American Film and Television
courses.description: Lecture, six hours. Survey of art of animation in America from its precinema origins to recent films of Disney, Pixar, DreamWorks, Ghibli, and others. Place of animation in pop culture, racial imagery and ethnic stereotypes, growth of art form, and how it reflects American society. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Intermediate Screenwriting Workshop
courses.description: Seminar, three hours. Problems in film and television writing. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Advanced Screenwriting Workshop
courses.description: Laboratory, three hours. Requisite: course 134. Course 135A is requisite to 135B, which is requisite to 135C. Course in film and television writing. First act of original screenplay to be developed. Letter grading.

courses.title: Advanced Screenwriting Workshop
courses.description: Laboratory, three hours. Requisite: course 135A. Limited to Film and Television majors. Designed for seniors. Course in film and television writing. Second act of original screenplay to be developed. Letter grading.

courses.title: Advanced Screenwriting Workshop
courses.description: Laboratory, three hours. Requisite: course 135B. Limited to Film and Television majors. Designed for seniors. Course in film and television writing. Third act of original screenplay to be developed. Letter grading.

courses.title: Cinematography
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, three hours. Requisite: course 101A. Corequisite: course 154. Limited to Film and Television majors. Introduction to motion imaging photography for thorough understanding of fundamental tools and principles of cinematography to create images that support and enhance story of film, achieve comprehension of principles of motion imaging… For more content click the Read More button below.

courses.title: Motion Picture Lighting
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, three hours. Enforced requisites: courses 52, 101A, 185. Limited to Film and Television majors. Introduction to principles and tools of lighting used in visual storytelling through lectures, discussions, and screenings. Creative lighting techniques covering topics such as people, environment, spatial relationships, movement, color, special effects, and… For more content click the Read More button below.

courses.title: Film Editing
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, two hours. Requisite: course 101A. Corequisite: course 150. Limited to Film and Television majors. Introduction to artistic and technical problems of film editing, with practical experience in editing of image and synchronous sound. Letter grading.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital Media and Tools
courses.description: Lecture, six hours; laboratory, one hour. Enforced requisite: course 101A. Limited to Film and Television majors. Instruction and exercises in basic concepts and software of virtual production environments and digital postproduction tools. Letter grading.

courses.title: Directing Cameras
courses.description: Laboratory, three hours. Enforced requisite: course 101A. Limited to Film and Television majors. Investigation of expressive potential of image within and beyond narrative from directorial perspective. Experiments with working methodologies that stimulate visual creativity and positioning image as fundamental element of cinematic expression. Letter grading.

courses.title: Undergraduate Film Production
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; laboratory, eight hours. Requisite: 185. Course 175A is requisite to 175B. Limited to Film and Television majors. Writing, preproduction, and production of short film not to exceed 12 minutes, including credits. Letter grading.

courses.title: Undergraduate Film Production
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, eight hours. Enforced requisite: course 175A. Limited to Film and Television majors. Completion of postproduction (editing, creation of sound tracks) for short film begun in course 175A. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Film and Television Production Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory, to be arranged. Supervised laboratory experience in various aspects of film and television production. May be repeated for maximum of 12 units, but only 8 units may be applied toward Film and Television major. Letter grading.

courses.title: Corporate Internships in Film, Television, and Digital Media
courses.description: Tutorial, one hour; internship, eight hours. Limited to juniors/seniors. Corporate internship in supervised setting in business related to film, television, and digital media industries. Students meet on regular basis with instructor and provide periodic reports of their experience. May be repeated for credit. Individual contract with supervising faculty member required.… For more content click the Read More button below.

courses.title: Introductory Screenwriting
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for course C132/C430. Structural analysis of feature films and development of professional screenwriters’ vocabulary for constructing, deconstructing, and reconstructing their own work. Screenings of films and selected film sequences in class and by assignment. P/NP or… For more content click the Read More button below.

courses.title: Introduction to Art and Technique of Filmmaking
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour. Students acquire understanding of practical and aesthetic challenges undertaken by artists and professionals in making of motion pictures and television. Examination of film as both art and industry: storytelling, sound and visual design, casting and performance, editing, finance, advertising, and distribution. courses.title: Digital Media Studies
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, one hour. Introduction to history, theory, and authoring skills of digital media, art, and culture. P/NP or Letter grading.

courses.title: History of American Motion Picture
courses.description: Lecture/screenings, six hours; discussion, one hour. Historical and critical survey, with examples, of American motion picture both as developing art form and as medium of mass communication. Letter grading.

courses.title: Overview of Contemporary Film Industry
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Examination of evolving economic structures and business practices in contemporary Hollywood film industry, with emphasis on operations of studios and independent distribution companies, their development, marketing, and distribution systems, and their relationship to independent producers, talent, and agencies. Letter grading.

courses.title: Intermediate Cinematography
courses.description: Lecture, two hours; laboratory, four hours. Enforced requisite: course 101A. Intermediate study of principles of cinematography, with emphasis on exposure, lighting, and selection of film, camera, and lenses. Concurrently scheduled with course C416. Letter grading.

courses.title: Lighting for Film and Television
courses.description: Lecture, two hours; laboratory, six hours. Requisite: course 52. Limited to Film and Television majors. courses.title: Digital Workflow
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, two hours. Requisites: courses 52, 185. Limited to departmental majors. Through discussions, demonstrations, outside speakers, and laboratory assignments, demystification of ever-changing world of digital workflow. Students plan, schedule, and budget their overall workflow in preproduction. May be repeated once for credit. courses.title: Introduction to Animation
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, three hours. Drawing experience not required. Fundamentals of animation through preparation of short animated film. Concurrently scheduled with course C481A. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Writing for Animation
courses.description: Lecture, six hours; studio, to be arranged. Requisite: course C181A or consent of instructor. Research and practice in creative writing and planning for animated film. May be repeated for maximum of 16 units. Concurrently scheduled with course C481B. P/NP or letter grading.
courses.prereqs_raw: Requisite: course C181A or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Animation Workshop
courses.description: Studio, six hours. Preparation: storyboard at first class meeting. Requisite: course C181A. Organization and integration of various creative arts used in animation to form complete study of selected topic. May be repeated for maximum of 16 units. Concurrently scheduled with course C481C. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Women and Film
courses.description: (Same as Gender Studies M111.) Lecture, eight hours; discussion, one hour. Historical issues and critical approaches to women and cinema that may include authorship, stardom, female genres, and images of women in Hollywood cinema, alternative cinema, and independent cinema from silent era to present. Letter grading.

courses.title: Chicanos in Film/Video
courses.description: (Same as Chicana/o and Central American Studies M114.) Lecture/screenings, five hours; discussion, one hour. Goal is to gain nuanced understanding of Chicano cinema as political, socioeconomic, cultural, and aesthetic practice. courses.title: Introduction to Theater
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour (when scheduled). Exploration of theater in production, with emphasis on collaborative role of theater artists and active role of audience. courses.title: Introduction to Directing
courses.description: Lecture, two hours; studio, four hours. Investigation of role of director in theatrical production and theories of play direction, with emphasis on analysis and interpretation of dramatic work and its realization in production. Letter grading.

courses.title: Acting Fundamentals
courses.description: Studio, four hours. Introduction to interpretation of drama through art of actor. Development of individual insights, skills, and disciplines in presentation of dramatic material to audiences. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Acting, Voice, and Movement Workshop I
courses.description: Studio, three to six hours. Study of beginning acting technique, scene study, and development of voice and movement skills. May be repeated for maximum of 12 units. Letter grading.

courses.title: Acting, Voice, and Movement Workshop I
courses.description: Studio, three to six hours. Study of beginning acting technique, scene study, and development of voice and movement skills. May be repeated for maximum of 12 units. Letter grading.

courses.title: Acting, Voice, and Movement Workshop I
courses.description: Studio, three to six hours. Study of beginning acting technique, scene study, and development of voice and movement skills. May be repeated for maximum of 12 units. Letter grading.

courses.title: Dramatic Writing
courses.description: Studio, three hours. Intended for Theater minors and other nonmajors. Exploration and development of creative writing skills for one or more of various forms of entertainment media. May be repeated once. Letter grading.
